\[
\frac{\partial L}{\partial t} = \operatorname{div}\big(g(\lvert \nabla L_\sigma \rvert)\, \nabla L\big),
\qquad
g = \frac{1}{1 + \lvert \nabla L_\sigma \rvert^2 / k^2} \text{ (Perona-Malik g2)},
\qquad
R = L_{xx} L_{yy} - L_{xy}^2
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(L\): The image as it diffuses over time t
- \(g\): The conductance, small at strong edges
- \(k\): The contrast factor
- \(R\): The determinant of the Hessian
- \(x, y\): The keypoint position, with the center of the top-left pixel at 0, 0
- \(\theta\): The orientation, counterclockwise from the x axis

A Gaussian scale space blurs edges as much as flat areas. AKAZE instead lets the image diffuse with a conductance g that falls where the gradient is large, so edges stay sharp. The contrast factor k comes from the gradients of the image. Fast explicit diffusion solves the equation in steps of varying length, which is much faster than the implicit scheme of KAZE. Keypoints are maxima of the determinant of the Hessian, with derivatives scaled to each level, above the threshold. The orientation is the dominant direction of the first derivatives in a circle around the keypoint, found with a sliding window of 60 degrees. The Inspector shows the formula of the chosen diffusivity.
